newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P rates Beijing Expressways senior notes BB.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Beijing Expressways senior notes BB.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Tuesday it had assigned its BB long-term rating to Greater Beijing First Expressways' US$100 million senior notes due 2004 and its US$175 million senior notes due 2007.
The outlook is stable, S&P said.
The company holds interests through Sino-joint ventures in five expressway projects in the greater Beijing area of the People's Republic of China.
Of the company's three operating expressways, two projects form part of the Beijing-Shenzhen Expressway and one project forms part of the Beijing-Shanghai Expressway, S&P said.
It said there are two expressways under advanced development, which will form sections of the Beijing-Shenyang Expressway.
The company will use the proceeds of the note issues to fund capital commitments for operationg roads and to fund construction and other costs in roads under development.

S&P said the ratings reflects the following risks: traffic volume risk, toll increase pricing risk, construction completion risk, and the higher regulatory risk inherent in the structuring of the projects into smaller-sized separate joint ventures.

S&P also said that the company's prospective cash flow in early years with high capital expenditure shows weak interest coverages. This is mitigated by an interim reserve to cover two six-month debt service periods, and a six-month debt service reserve throughout the life of the bonds.
S&P said the rating also reflects the following strengths:
The projected financial profile of the company is strong for the rating category, based on conservative traffic and toll projections.
The company's expressways exhibit strong underlying economic fundamentals.

As part of an immature and emerging highway network in northern China, the expressways are not currently exposed to competing roads of the same quality, and therefore are not subject to the same degree of bypass risk as is seen in many countries or regions.

The company has the right to receive a significant share of distributable profits as well as shareholder loan repayments from the joint ventures, which are well defined through a flow of fund mechanism in the joint venture contracts.

The company's parent, Greater Beijing Region Expressways Ltd has provided a contingent support agreement to provide up to US$50 million to the company to help fund completion of the projects under development, which enhances the financial flexibility of the company during its development stage.
